newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan may tender for 200,000t beans/70,000t corn.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan may tender for 200,000t beans/70,000t corn.

text.p: Falling grains and oilseeds futures prices in the U.S. could prompt Taiwan to tender for 200,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 70,000 tonnes of U.S. corn in the next two weeks, Taiwan traders said on Friday.
Taiwan's Breakfast Soybeans Procurement Association's Taichung division may tender within two weeks for two 54,000-tonne shipments of U.S. soybeans, the traders said.
The group's Kaohsiung division is also expected to place a tender for a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. soybeans, they added.
Both soybean buying divisions are expecting soybean futures price to drop below US$7 per bushel in the near term because of prospects for a bumper U.S. harvest.
The November contract in the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) closed 2-1/2 U.S. cents down to $6.88-1/2 a bushel.
"U.S. soybean could drop to test its support between $6.70 to US$6.80 per bushel before the harvest season ends in November," a Formosa Oilseeds executive said.
Taiwan's Flour Mills Association would remain sidelined in the week of Oct 20 after it bought two shipments totaling 60,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat on October 11, an official said.
The local flour price listed on Friday ranged between T$14.55 to T$15.68 kg for Taipei delivery, unchanged from a week earlier.

Buyers said pressures from the ample U.S. corn harvest could also push corn prices below $2.80 per bushel and test support at $2.70 per bushel. The December CBOT contract closed on Thursday unchanged at $2.83-1/4 a bushel.
"Corn will remain bearish until mid-November when the harvest season ends," a buyer with the Feed Industry Group said.
Taiwan's FGEP corn buying group is expected to retender within two weeks for 54,000 tonnes of U.S. corn, traders said.
The FGEP shipment would be slated for delivery from December 10-25 from the U.S. Gulf or December 26 to January 9 from the Pacific Northwest, traders said.

Taiwan's Hui Shung Group is also expected to tender for a combined shipment of 16,000 tonnes of corn and 38,000 tonnes of soybeans, traders said. The Hui Shung Group's shipment would be slated for delivery in March.
Taiwan's soymeal price on Friday for Taipei delivery was quoted at T$9.70-$9.90 a kg, unchanged from last week.
The price of corn powders was at T$7.10 per kg for Taipei delivery, down from $7.12 per kg a week earlier.
Local Pacific Northwest freight cost was about US$10.50 per tonne and the Gulf of Mexico is about US$18.00-$19.00 per tonne, both for Panamax-sized January and February shipments.
